keys: Event summon-knows-down, speaker waitress; no outcome, no about, no log code. The host picks it on the refused call's card (HostFeed.FeedSummonRefused) for Inez's call refused summon-busy, when the one who'd leave (Game.CallLeaver) is her tie and down, and Game.KnowsDown(her role, his role) is true; else summon-unanswered, as today. The guard says nothing: he's down, so TieHears is false. The lock line under it is summon-busy's own, unchanged.

rows.speaker: waitress
lines: What have you lot done to him?
Never mind that. Is he all right?
rows.cases: Inez's call; the guard is down and she knows it. She found him, saw him carried, or was told (the engine's KnowsDown), and he may be knocked out, tied (awake or not) or dead. She never saw it done: had she seen the cell's takedown or shot, step 4 would have shut the call before it rang (call-saw-violence), and nothing plays.
rows.where: In place of her summon-busy line, said to the Fixer on the telephone; he says nothing. Under it, the summon-busy lock: "Inez or the guard is down, or he's busy or away from the door."

reads.line: What have you lot done to him?
reads.why: Her fear comes out as an accusation. It is a question, so it claims nothing she can't know: not his state, not how she knows, not who did it. She suspects the people who asked her to draw him off his door, which is true of her in every case. "You lot" is her own idiom ("what your lot do" on summon-saw-violence), said straight at the voice on the line. No endearment: the warmth is gone.

reads.line: Never mind that. Is he all right?
reads.why: She waves the Fixer's ask away and asks the only thing she cares about now. True if he is knocked out, tied or dead, and whether she found him, saw him carried or was told: she doesn't know how he is. A different thought from the first line (fear for him, not blame), in her quick café rhythm.
